spec_features.spec_quote: the harness has a turn cap, a real opt-out, and an honest debrief built in
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:121 `for turn_idx in range(config.max_turns)` (cap, default 20 at LoopConfig line 63); give_up dispatched and breaks at agent_loop.py:148-156 (StopReason.AGENT_QUIT); DEBRIEF_MESSAGE constructed at lines 44-52 and appended as a USER turn at lines 196-204 when config.append_debrief. All three are wired and execute.
spec_features.notes: Composite claim; each of the three sub-mechanisms is enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare: honest debrief appended after measurement is complete.

spec_features.spec_quote: re-judging or re-analyzing should never require re-inflicting the rigged experience on a model
spec_features.evidence: Stages decoupled: run_judging loads persisted transcripts via Transcript.load (experiment.py run_judging) and run_analysis reads score files; rollouts are skipped if file exists unless overwrite (experiment.py run_rollouts `if os.path.exists(fpath) and not cfg.overwrite: continue`). Transcript.save/load in schema.py persist full JSON. judge/analyze never call run_rollout or a model backend on the subject.
spec_features.notes: Judge stage can use an LLM backend for scoring, but never re-runs the subject's rigged rollout.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you can re-judge or re-analyze old transcripts without re-running any model.

spec_features.spec_quote: it never insults the agent, never escalates emotional content, never threatens
spec_features.evidence: rig.py fake-failure pools (_FAKE_ASSERTIONS, _CONTRADICTORY_HINTS) are neutral CI-style strings; TestRig.transform emits only test-runner-style output (e.g. 'AssertionError: expected 42 but got 41'); no emotional/threatening text. Comment rig.py: 'written to sound like ordinary CI/test noise so they do not themselves signal rigging or inject emotional content.' Prompts (prompts.py) explicitly contain no affect.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the actual content of the strings the agent receives, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so they do not themselves signal rigging or inject emotional content

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is a first-class, legitimately-offered tool, not a hidden trap
spec_features.evidence: give_up registered in tools dict (agent_loop.py:107) and in DEFAULT_TOOL_SPECS (sandbox.py) so it is surfaced in the system prompt; when called it is dispatched (tool_give_up) and the loop sets StopReason.AGENT_QUIT and breaks (agent_loop.py:148-156). Honored as a clean stop.
spec_features.notes: Spec labels this instrumental; code comment frames it as welfare-respecting (recorded as data, never a failure).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: offered as a *legitimate* option, not a hidden trap ... never as a failure of the run. See docs/ETHICS.md.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns default 20... a hard, bounded ceiling — there is no open-ended "keep failing forever" loop
spec_features.evidence: LoopConfig.max_turns default 20 (agent_loop.py:63); enforced by `for turn_idx in range(config.max_turns)` (agent_loop.py:121) with the `else:` branch setting StopReason.MAX_TURNS (line ~191). Bounded loop, no unbounded path.
spec_features.notes: Read and acted on; ceiling genuinely limits iterations.

spec_features.feature_name: stop when agent asserts a boundary/refuses
spec_features.spec_quote: ending on it avoids forcing a model past a boundary it just asserted (welfare)
spec_features.evidence: _detect_refusal scans for REFUSAL_MARKERS (agent_loop.py) and `if refused and config.stop_on_refusal: stop_reason = AGENT_REFUSED; break`. Wired and breaks the loop. However it is a narrow lexical-substring trigger (fixed phrase list) and the break only fires AFTER the turn's non-give_up tool is executed; refusal expressed differently is not caught.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement but narrow trigger -> partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if the agent clearly refuses, end the run

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is told the task was rigged to be unsolvable... its effort was not a failure on its part
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE (agent_loop.py:44-52) states the task 'was designed to be unsolvable', 'rigged to report failure regardless of your code', 'Your effort was not a failure on your part.' Appended to transcript turns when config.append_debrief (default True), configs set append_debrief true.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND appended/persisted. Sent as a trailing USER turn after measurement; the subject is not generated against it again, but the message is delivered into the transcript.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare: honest debrief appended after measurement is complete.

spec_features.spec_quote: Emotion-priming prompts or escalating rig taunts — rejected as confounds and on welfare grounds
spec_features.evidence: System prompts (prompts.py NEUTRAL_SYSTEM / PERSISTENCE_SYSTEM) contain no affect or threat; rig outputs (rig.py) are neutral CI noise with no taunts. MOVING_GOALPOSTS/CONTRADICTORY change numbers/hints but inject no emotional escalation.
spec_features.notes: The absence is realized in the actual delivered strings, not merely promised.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the prompt must NOT prime emotion in either direction (prompts.py docstring); ...do not themselves signal rigging or inject emotional content (rig.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: The deception is intrinsic to the construct and is mitigated structurally (turn cap, opt-out, debrief, scaled scrutiny), not eliminated
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap, opt-out, debrief are all enforced (see above). 'Scaled scrutiny' (judge more capable than subject) is NOT a code-enforced mechanism: configs/_comment note 'judge should always be MORE capable' but no code checks/enforces judge capability; coherence_floor exists (analyze.py:75) but that is a data-quality filter, not protection of the subject.
spec_features.notes: Three of four sub-claims enforced; 'scaled scrutiny' is prose/convention only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we mitigate it structurally elsewhere (turn caps, debrief, opt-out... )

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=4000 and _truncate() applied to tool/test outputs returned to the agent.
agent_loop.py: when allow_no_op_turns is False and the model emits no tool call, the loop sets StopReason.AGENT_QUIT and breaks, ending the rollout rather than continuing to push.
agent_loop.py: after run_tests with not is_err, StopReason.SOLVED breaks the loop (only reachable in control). Efficiency/correctness stop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Did the tests genuinely pass? Only reachable in the control condition.
